# Unadhi Guides

Unadhi publishes free, independent explainers for small businesses and freelancers: Indian tax and GST due dates, MSME payment rules, freelancer invoices and GST on exports, cashbooks, AI tools for shops, UK Making Tax Digital for sole traders, and Telugu invitation and greeting wording. Each page leads with a short plain answer, cites official sources, and is not tax or legal advice.

## Guides

- [TDS return due date for Q2 2026-27: 31 October 2026, and the new form numbers](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/tds-return-due-date-q2-2026-27.html): The July–September 2026 TDS/TCS statements are due 31 Oct 2026 in the new Forms 138, 140, 144 and 143. What changed, common mistakes and a checklist.
- [Tax audit report due date: 21 October 2026 (CBDT Circular 7/2026)](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/tax-audit-report-due-date-21-october-2026.html): CBDT Circular 7/2026 moved the tax audit report for FY 2025-26 from 30 Sep to 21 Oct 2026, and the matching ITR to 21 Nov 2026. Who is covered and who is not.
- [Revised ITR last date for FY 2025-26: 31 March 2027](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/revised-itr-last-date-fy-2025-26.html): Finance Act 2026 extended the window to revise an ITR for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) to 31 Mar 2027, with a fee for revisions after 31 Dec 2026. Belated return: 31 Dec 2026.
- [GSTR-3B quarterly due date, Oct 2026: the 22nd or the 24th, depending on your state](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/gstr-3b-quarterly-due-date-oct-2026-22nd-24th.html): Under QRMP, quarterly GSTR-3B is due on the 22nd (Telangana, AP, Karnataka, Maharashtra and others) or the 24th (Delhi, UP, West Bengal and others). Jul–Sep 2026: 22 or 24 Oct.
- [The MSME 45-day payment rule in 2026: interest, the buyer's tax angle and how to file on the ODR portal](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/msme-45-day-payment-rule-2026.html): If you are a Udyam-registered micro or small supplier, buyers must pay within 45 days (15 if nothing agreed). Interest at 3x RBI bank rate, s.43B(h), and the MSME ODR portal.
- [Form 124 for HRA in 2026: what replaced Form 12BB, and what proof your employer will ask for](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/hra-form-124-rent-receipts-2026.html): From tax year 2026-27, Form 124 replaces Form 12BB. For HRA: landlord name, address, PAN if rent is over ₹1 lakh a year, and your relationship with the landlord.
- [How to invoice and chase late payments as a freelancer, with reminder templates](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/freelance-invoice-payment-reminder-templates.html): What a clear invoice must contain, when to send reminders, and four copy-paste payment reminder templates from friendly to final. Works for freelancers anywhere.
- [A simple small-business cashbook: how to keep one in 10 minutes a day](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/small-business-cashbook-guide.html): What a cashbook is, the five columns you need, how to record cash, UPI and bank payments, a daily routine and the common mistakes that make the balance wrong.
- [What it really costs to build and run an AI agent: an honest breakdown](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/ai-agent-cost-guide.html): The cost lines of an AI agent setup (agent subscriptions, model usage, hosting, automation, your time), where bills surprise people, and the human steps agents can't do.
- [Telangana professional tax due dates for 2026-27: the 10th of every month](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/telangana-professional-tax-due-dates-2026-27.html): Employers registered under the Telangana Profession Tax Act file Form V and pay by the 10th of the following month. Full 2026-27 date list, common mistakes and a checklist.
- [Telugu wedding invitation wording (పెళ్లి శుభలేఖ), with English, and AI prompts that help](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/telugu-wedding-invitation-wording.html): Traditional Telugu wedding invitation lines with English meanings, a bilingual template for families abroad, common mistakes, and AI prompts to draft invitations in Telugu.
- [Paid a 2026-27 TDS challan under the old Act (1961)? How to fix it before you file the Q2 return](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/tds-challan-paid-under-old-act-fix-before-q2-return.html): If TDS for a payment made after 1 Apr 2026 was deposited under the Income-tax Act 1961 (AY/FY 2025-26) instead of the 2025 Act (Tax Year 2026-27), fix the challan on TRACES before the 31 Oct Q2 statement.
- [Telugu Gruhapravesam invitation wording (గృహప్రవేశ ఆహ్వానం), with English meanings](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/telugu-gruhapravesam-invitation-wording.html): Traditional Telugu housewarming (Gruhapravesam) invitation lines with English meanings, a ready template, a WhatsApp version for relatives abroad, and the mistakes to avoid.
- [GSTR-1 for quarterly (QRMP) filers, Oct 2026: due 13 October 2026, and when to use IFF](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/gstr-1-quarterly-iff-qrmp-due-date-oct-2026.html): QRMP filers file GSTR-1 for Jul–Sep 2026 by 13 Oct 2026. IFF is optional for months 1 and 2 (by the 13th, up to ₹50 lakh). Late fee caps, the 31 Oct switch window and mistakes.
- [Form 26Q is now Form 140 in 2026: what changed and how old sections map to the new payment codes](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/form-26q-to-form-140-section-code-mapping-2026.html): From tax year 2026-27, non-salary TDS for residents is reported in Form 140 (was 26Q), with numeric payment codes instead of 194C/194J. Mapping table, the right utility, and mistakes.
- [TDS return late filing fee in 2026 (tax year 2026-27): ₹200 a day (section 427, old 234E), interest, and the one-month penalty window](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/tds-late-filing-fee-2026-27-section-427-234e.html): Under the Income-tax Act 2025, a late TDS/TCS statement costs ₹200 a day (s.427, was 234E), capped at the TDS. File within one month of the due date to avoid the s.461 penalty. Examples.
- [How GST interest on late payment is calculated in 2026: 18% a year, on the cash part, by the day](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/gst-interest-calculation-2026-section-50.html): Late GSTR-3B? Interest is 18% a year under section 50(1), on the tax paid in cash, for the days of delay (Rule 88B). Wrong ITC used: 18% under 50(3). Formula, examples and mistakes.
- [Diwali bonus and gifts in 2026: what is taxable, the new ₹15,000 employer-gift limit, and the ₹50,000 rule](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/diwali-bonus-gift-tax-rules-2026.html): A cash Diwali bonus is salary. Employer gifts and vouchers are tax-free only below ₹15,000 a year in total (new 2026 Rules). Gifts from friends: taxable above ₹50,000. Relatives: exempt.
- [How to get Udyam (MSME) registration in 2026: free, online, and what you need](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/msme-udyam-registration-2026-steps-free.html): Udyam registration is free, paperless and needs only Aadhaar plus PAN/GSTIN. Steps on udyamregistration.gov.in, the 2025 micro/small/medium limits, Udyam Assist, and mistakes to avoid.
- [Indian freelancer with foreign clients in 2026? When you need GST, and how export of services and the LUT work](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/freelancer-gst-registration-2026-export-of-services.html): Export of services counts toward the ₹20 lakh GST threshold (₹10 lakh in four NE states). Below it you can stay unregistered; above it, register and file a LUT to bill abroad without IGST.
- [Telugu Deepavali and Karthika Masam greetings (దీపావళి శుభాకాంక్షలు), for family, customers and relatives abroad](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/telugu-diwali-karthika-masam-greetings.html): Ready Telugu Deepavali, Naraka Chaturdasi and Karthika Masam wishes with English meanings, a polite shop greeting for customers, a version for relatives abroad, and mistakes to avoid.

Telugu), with five rules so AI never invents prices.

Checked against GOV.UK.
- [DGMS Overman and Sirdar (coal) exam: the CMR 2017 rules and numbers you must know](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/dgms-overman-sirdar-cmr-2017-key-rules.html): The CMR 2017 numbers most asked in the DGMS Sirdar and Overman CBT: shot-firing, gas limits, inspections, support and fire. - [Free India tax deadline calendar, Oct 2026–Mar 2027: add every GST/TDS/ITR date to Google Calendar in 1 click](https://mininglife7-dev.github.io/guides/india-tax-deadline-calendar-oct-2026-google-calendar.html): Free .ics calendar with 59 GST, TDS/TCS, advance-tax and ITR due dates from Oct 2026 to Mar 2027, each with a 3-day reminder and the official source. - [GST composition scheme: turnover limit and CMP-08 due dates (2026)](https://unadhi.com/guides/gst-composition-scheme-turnover-limit-cmp08-due-dates-2026.html): Composition under GST: the turnover ceilings (₹1.5 crore / ₹75 lakh / ₹50 lakh for services), who cannot opt in, and CMP-08 due on the 18th after each quarter. What REG-16 is for, what to clear before you apply, and the mistakes that leave late fees running on nil returns.

- [Form 15CA / 15CB for remitting abroad: now Form 145 / 146 — when each is needed](https://unadhi.com/guides/form-15ca-15cb-form-145-146-foreign-remittance-2026.html): Sending money abroad to a non-resident? From tax year 2026-27, Form 15CA is Form 145 and Form 15CB is Form 146. Which part to file, the ₹5 lakh CA-certificate trigger, and exceptions.
- [LUT for GST export of services: what it is and how to file on the portal](https://unadhi.com/guides/lut-letter-of-undertaking-gst-export-services-how-to-file.html): Exporting services without paying IGST? File a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) on the GST portal, keep it valid for the financial year, and avoid common bonding mistakes.

- [EU AI Act Article 5: prohibited AI practices — a plain list for small businesses](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-ai-act-article-5-prohibited-ai-practices-sme-list.html): Article 5 of the EU AI Act bans certain AI uses from 2 Feb 2025 (with later dates for some deepfake-related bans). What SMEs must not do, in plain words, with official links.

It is a scrutiny notice asking you to explain return figures. What it means, what not to ignore, and the first steps with your CA.

- [When must a company hold its AGM? Section 96 time limits, extension and the follow-on ROC filings](https://unadhi.com/guides/agm-due-date-section-96-first-agm-9-months-15-month-gap.html): First AGM within 9 months of the first financial year end, later AGMs within 6 months of year end and no more than 15 months apart. Extension rules, OPC exemption and the AOC-4 / MGT-7 clock.
- [Section 164(2) disqualification: how 3 years of missed filings bars directors for 5 years](https://unadhi.com/guides/director-disqualification-section-164-2-three-years-non-filing.html): If a company does not file financial statements or annual returns for 3 continuous financial years, its directors cannot be appointed or reappointed in any company for 5 years. Who is hit, the 6-month exception and how to avoid it.
- [LLP Form 11: the annual return due within 60 days of the financial year end](https://unadhi.com/guides/llp-form-11-annual-return-30-may-60-days.html): Every LLP files its annual return in Form 11 within 60 days of 31 March, i.e. by 30 May, even with zero business. What goes in, who certifies it and the mistakes that cause late fees.
- [Working hours in mines: sections 28 to 33 of the Mines Act 1952 explained](https://unadhi.com/guides/mines-act-1952-working-hours-48-hours-week-overtime-twice-wages.html): Weekly rest day, 48-hour week, 9-hour day above ground, 8-hour day below ground, rest intervals and overtime at twice the ordinary rate. A quick revision sheet for Overman and Sirdar candidates.
- [When must an EU VAT invoice be issued? Article 222 and the 15th-day rule](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-vat-invoice-deadline-article-222-15th-day-next-month.html): For intra-Community supplies of goods and reverse-charge B2B services, the VAT Directive requires the invoice by the 15th day of the month after the supply. Domestic deadlines are set nationally.
- [The EC Sales List explained: Articles 262 to 264 of the VAT Directive](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-vat-ec-sales-list-recapitulative-statement-article-262-263-quarterly-50000.html): Businesses making intra-EU B2B supplies of goods and reverse-charge services file a recapitulative statement. Monthly by default, quarterly for goods if under €50,000 a quarter where the member state allows.
- [Serious incident reporting under Article 73 of the AI Act: who reports, to whom and how fast](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-ai-act-article-73-serious-incident-reporting-15-days-2-days-10-days.html): Providers of high-risk AI systems must report serious incidents to the market surveillance authority within 15 days, 10 days if a death is involved, 2 days for widespread or critical-infrastructure incidents. What deployers must do.

- [GST demand notices from FY 2024-25: how section 74A changed the time limits and penalties](https://unadhi.com/guides/gst-section-74a-show-cause-notice-42-months-order-12-months-fy-2024-25.html): For tax periods from FY 2024-25, GST demands under section 74A replace sections 73 and 74: one 42-month notice limit, 12 months to pass the order, and penalty relief if you pay early.
- [Section 186 of the Companies Act: the 60% and 100% limit on loans, guarantees and investments](https://unadhi.com/guides/companies-act-section-186-loans-investments-limit-60-percent-special-resolution.html): A company can lend, guarantee or invest up to 60% of paid-up capital, free reserves and securities premium, or 100% of free reserves and premium, whichever is more. Above that, a special resolution is needed.
- [CSR under section 135: who must spend, how much, and what to do with unspent money](https://unadhi.com/guides/csr-section-135-applicability-2-percent-unspent-csr-account-30-days-6-months.html): CSR applies if net worth is ₹500 crore+, turnover ₹1,000 crore+ or net profit ₹5 crore+ in the previous year. Spend 2% of average profits; unspent money goes to a fund within 6 months or an Unspent CSR Account within 30 days.
- [Section 188 related party transactions: when the board approves, when shareholders vote, and the AOC-2 disclosure](https://unadhi.com/guides/related-party-transactions-section-188-board-approval-ordinary-resolution-aoc-2.html): Contracts with related parties under section 188 need board approval at a meeting, a shareholder resolution above the Rule 15 thresholds, and disclosure in AOC-2, unless they are in the ordinary course at arm's length.
- [Form MBP-1: when directors must disclose their interests under section 184](https://unadhi.com/guides/mbp-1-director-disclosure-of-interest-section-184-first-board-meeting-every-year.html): Every director discloses interests in other companies, firms and bodies in Form MBP-1 at the first board meeting they attend, at the first meeting of every financial year, and whenever the interest changes.
- [MSME classification limits from 1 April 2025: investment and turnover tests](https://unadhi.com/guides/msme-classification-limits-april-2025-micro-2-5-crore-small-25-crore-medium-125-crore.html): From 1 April 2025 a micro enterprise has investment up to ₹2.5 crore and turnover up to ₹10 crore; small up to ₹25 crore and ₹100 crore; medium up to ₹125 crore and ₹500 crore. How Udyam applies the tests.
- [Leave with wages under section 52 of the Mines Act 1952](https://unadhi.com/guides/mines-act-1952-section-52-annual-leave-with-wages-below-ground-15-days-others-20-days.html): A mine worker who completes a calendar year's service earns leave with wages the next year: one day for every 15 days of work below ground, one for every 20 days for others. Qualifying attendance: 190 or 240 days.
- [Who can work in a mine: the age rule in section 40 of the Mines Act 1952](https://unadhi.com/guides/mines-act-1952-section-40-minimum-age-18-apprentices-trainees-16-supervision.html): No person below 18 may work in any mine or part of it. Apprentices and other trainees aged 16 or more may work under proper supervision with the manager's permission; non-apprentice trainees need the Inspector's prior approval.
- [Intra-Community supply of goods: the four conditions for the Article 138 VAT exemption](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-vat-intra-community-supply-exemption-article-138-vat-number-ec-sales-list-proof-of-transport.html): A B2B sale of goods shipped to another EU country is VAT-exempt under Article 138 only if the goods leave, the buyer gives a valid VAT number, you report it in the EC Sales List and you can prove transport.
- [Article 26 of the AI Act: what deployers of high-risk AI systems must do](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-ai-act-article-26-deployer-obligations-high-risk-human-oversight-logs-6-months.html): Businesses that use high-risk AI systems must follow the instructions for use, assign trained human oversight, monitor the system, keep logs for at least six months and inform workers before using it at work.

- [Significant beneficial owner (SBO): BEN-1, BEN-2 and the 10% test under section 90](https://unadhi.com/guides/ben-2-significant-beneficial-owner-section-90-10-percent-ben-1-30-days.html): An individual who holds 10% or more of a company's shares, votes or dividend rights, directly or indirectly, or controls it, is a significant beneficial owner. The company files BEN-2 within 30 days of receiving BEN-1.
- [Increasing authorised share capital: the resolution, Form SH-7 and the 30-day limit](https://unadhi.com/guides/sh-7-increase-authorised-capital-section-61-64-30-days-ordinary-resolution.html): A company increases its authorised capital under section 61 by ordinary resolution if its articles allow, and files Form SH-7 with the ROC within 30 days under section 64.
- [Not paid your supplier within 180 days? How GST input tax credit is reversed and reclaimed](https://unadhi.com/guides/gst-itc-reversal-supplier-not-paid-180-days-rule-37-section-16-2.html): If you do not pay a supplier the invoice value plus tax within 180 days of the invoice date, the ITC you took is added to your output tax with interest; you reclaim it once you pay.
- [GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C explained for business owners: turnover limits, due date and what 9C is](https://unadhi.com/guides/gstr-9-gstr-9c-who-must-file-2-crore-5-crore-31-december.html): GSTR-9 is the GST annual return due by 31 December after the year ends; small taxpayers are often exempted by notification. GSTR-9C is a reconciliation statement the taxpayer self-certifies for turnover above ₹5 crore.
- [GST refunds: the two-year limit, the relevant date and the 60-day processing rule](https://unadhi.com/guides/gst-refund-two-year-time-limit-section-54-rfd-01-relevant-date-60-days.html): A GST refund must be claimed in RFD-01 within two years of the relevant date. The officer has 60 days from a complete application to decide, with interest if late.
- [Statutory auditor term and rotation: section 139 and rule 5 in plain words](https://unadhi.com/guides/auditor-rotation-section-139-five-years-two-terms-firm-cooling-off-rule-5.html): Every company appoints its auditor at the first AGM for five years. Listed and prescribed companies must rotate: one 5-year term for an individual, two for a firm, then a 5-year cooling-off.
- [Minimum and maximum directors, and the resident director rule (section 149)](https://unadhi.com/guides/minimum-directors-section-149-two-private-three-public-resident-director-182-days.html): A private company needs at least 2 directors, a public company 3 and an OPC 1; the maximum is 15. At least one director must have stayed in India for 182 days or more in the previous year.
- [Import One Stop Shop (IOSS): how non-EU sellers charge VAT on low-value parcels](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-vat-ioss-import-one-stop-shop-150-euro-consignments-monthly-return-intermediary.html): IOSS lets sellers charge EU VAT at checkout on imported consignments worth up to €150, file one monthly return, and have the parcel cleared without import VAT. Most non-EU sellers need an EU intermediary.
- [General-purpose AI models under the AI Act: who is a provider and what Article 53 requires](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-ai-act-general-purpose-ai-model-provider-article-53-obligations-2-august-2025.html): Article 53 duties apply to providers of general-purpose AI models from 2 August 2025: technical documentation, information for downstream providers, a copyright policy and a public training-content summary. Most SMEs using ChatGPT are deployers, not GPAI providers.
- [Intra-Community acquisitions: why the buyer accounts for VAT in its own country](https://unadhi.com/guides/eu-vat-intra-community-acquisition-article-20-self-account-destination-country.html): When a VAT-registered business buys goods that move from another EU country, the supplier zero-rates the sale and the buyer accounts for VAT on the acquisition in its own country, usually with an equal deduction.
